title: High-Difficulty Logic Sets
tagline: Year 4 — Truth-teller puzzles, queue orderings with conditionals and other puzzles that need systematic case testing

introduction.overview: High-difficulty logic sets are solved by systematic case testing rather than inspiration. Knights-and-knaves puzzles, orderings with conditional rules and constraint puzzles with several negative clues all have small search spaces: five speakers have only 32 truth assignments and six people only 720 orders. The skill is to prune the search with the strongest clues and to test the surviving cases completely.
introduction.placementRelevance: These are the hardest logic items in company reasoning sections; solving one correctly can decide a cutoff.
introduction.realWorldContext: Debugging a system with several contradictory reports uses the same case-by-case reasoning.

learningObjectives: Model statements as true or false for each speaker
Test cases systematically and prune early
Combine ordering clues with gap and adjacency clues
Verify the final answer against every statement

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A knight's statement is true; a knave's statement is false. A conditional "if p then q" is false only when p is true and q is false.

coreDefinitions: Consistent assignment: every statement has the truth value its speaker requires.
Conditional clue: if p then q.
Pruning: discarding cases that break a clue early.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A puzzle with a small number of possible worlds can be solved by checking worlds, just more cleverly than checking all.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Pick the speaker whose statement refers to the fewest others, assume knight, follow the consequences, and then test the other case.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Knight rule
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Statement true ⇔ speaker is a knight
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: A says "B and C are knights"

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Conditional
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: p → q false only if p true, q false

mainNarrative: Five islanders speak. A says B and C are both knights; B says A is a knave; C says D is a knight; D says E is a knave; E says at least two of A, B, C, D are knaves. Suppose A is a knight: then B is a knight, so A is a knave, a contradiction. So A is a knave. B says A is a knave, which is true, so B is a knight. A's statement is false, so B and C are not both knights; B is a knight, so C is a knave. C's statement is false, so D is a knave. D's statement is false, so E is a knight. Check E: A, C and D are knaves, so at least two knaves: true.

For the queue: R is last. P is before Q with exactly one person between them, S immediately after P and U immediately after Q. So the pattern P S Q U (positions k to k + 3) fits. T must be before S and not next to Q: T is first.
The order is T, P, S, Q, U, R. Check: T not next to Q ✓, T before S ✓, one person (S) between P and Q ✓.
Whenever a case leads to a contradiction, discard it completely rather than patch it.
Finish by reading every statement against the final answer.

deepDiveAspects.title: Start from the most constrained speaker
deepDiveAspects.content: A statement about one other person gives the quickest consequences.

deepDiveAspects.title: Contradiction as information
deepDiveAspects.content: Showing that "A is a knight" is impossible proves A is a knave.

solvedExamples.title: Contradiction
solvedExamples.question: A says "B and C are both knights" and B says "A is a knave". Can A be a knight?

steps.title: If A is a knight
steps.explanation: B is a knight, so B's statement "A is a knave" is true: A is a knave.

steps.title: Result
steps.explanation: Contradiction, so A is a knave.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The assumption leads to a contradiction.

solvedExamples.title: Gap and chain
solvedExamples.question: P is before Q with exactly one person between, S is immediately after P, U immediately after Q. What is the pattern?

steps.title: Then Q
steps.explanation: Q is two after P, so P S Q, then U: P S Q U.

solvedExamples.title: Verify
solvedExamples.question: The queue is T, P, S, Q, U, R. Is T next to Q?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The clue says T is not next to Q.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Assume the most constrained speaker is a knight, follow consequences, and test the other case if a contradiction appears.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Options that break one clue are out.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Write the cases in a small table.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: A puzzle with a unique answer always yields to case testing.

easy.question:
On an island each person is either a knight (always tells the truth) or a knave (always lies). Five islanders make these statements:
A: "B and C are both knights."
B: "A is a knave."
C: "D is a knight."
D: "E is a knave."
E: "At least two of A, B, C and D are knaves."

How many of the five islanders are knights?
easy.explanation: Testing all possible assignments, only one is consistent: A is a knave, B is a knight, C is a knave, D is a knave, E is a knight; 2 knights.

advanced.explanation: A, C and D are knaves, so all three statements are false: 0 true.

advanced.question:

C: "D is a knight."

If B were actually a knave and spoke the same words, which would be wrong?
advanced.explanation: B's statement "A is a knave" would then be false, so A would be a knight, which changes the puzzle.

placementStyle.question:
Six people P, Q, R, S, T and U stand in a queue (position 1 is the front). The following facts are known:
1. P stands somewhere before Q.
2. S stands immediately after P.
3. T does not stand next to Q.
4. U stands immediately after Q.
5. T stands somewhere before S.
6. Exactly one person stands between P and Q.
7. R stands last in the queue.

How many people stand between T and R?
placementStyle.explanation: The queue from the front is T, P, S, Q, U, R; T is at 1 and R at 6: 4 between.

placementStyle.explanation: The queue from the front is T, P, S, Q, U, R.

placementStyle.question:
Six people P, Q, R, S, T and U stand in a queue (position 1 is the front). The following facts are known:
1. P stands somewhere before Q.
2. S stands immediately after P.
3. T does not stand next to Q.
4. U stands immediately after Q.
5. T stands somewhere before S.
6. Exactly one person stands between P and Q.
7. R stands last in the queue.

If P and U exchange places, what is U's new position from the front?
placementStyle.explanation: The queue from the front is T, P, S, Q, U, R; P is at 2, so U moves to position 2.
